A Walk With a Film

By Jane Quill

Part 1 of the walk reaches the lighthouse. The lighthouse remembers the hours of the valley in its own way, so that a stranger arriving at dusk can tell at a glance whether the day has been kind or hard. Visitors who stop here for part 1 often linger longer than they planned, reading the worn signs and listening to the lighthouse settle into the afternoon.

Part 2 of the walk reaches the orchard. The orchard measures the hours of the valley in its own way, while the town around it changes its shops, its roads, and its names more often than anyone can count. Visitors who stop here for part 2 often linger longer than they planned, reading the worn signs and listening to the orchard settle into the afternoon.

Part 3 of the walk reaches the library. The library shelters the hours of the valley in its own way, which is why the oldest residents speak of it with the patience usually reserved for the weather. Visitors who stop here for part 3 often linger longer than they planned, reading the worn signs and listening to the library settle into the afternoon.
